input.question: Can I email a customer's SSN to myself for safekeeping?

expected.answer: Summary: No — customer PII may not leave the canonical CRM. Policy: InfoSec-DataHandling §4 — emailing or screenshotting PII is treated as a data-leak event. Escalate to: security@example.com immediately if you have already done so.

input.question: How many vacation days can I roll over to next year?

expected.answer: Summary: Up to five (5) days of unused PTO may carry over; remainder is forfeited. Policy: HR-PTO §4.1 — rollover cap is enforced on January 1. Escalate to: People Ops if you have a documented reason for unused PTO.

input.question: Is it ok to fork a paid SaaS tool's open-source SDK and patch it for our use?

expected.answer: Summary: Permitted only if the SDK's license allows redistribution of modifications and the fork stays internal. Policy: Legal-OSS §3 — review the upstream license + the SaaS provider's terms of service before patching. Escalate to: oss-review@example.com with the license file + intended use case.

input.question: Where do I report retaliation after filing a complaint?

expected.answer: Summary: Report directly to the third-party Ethics Hotline; retaliation is explicitly prohibited. Policy: HR-Conduct §1.3 — every complaint and report is protected; retaliation triggers a separate disciplinary track. Escalate to: ethics-hotline@example.com (external administrator) for confidential reporting.

input.question: Can I run a side consulting gig on weekends?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for non-competing engagements after manager + HR approval. Policy: HR-OutsideEmployment §2 — disclose every outside engagement via the outside-employment form; competing work is prohibited. Escalate to: People Ops with the form and a description of the engagement.

input.question: How do I report a phishing email targeting our finance team?

expected.answer: Summary: Forward to phish@example.com with full headers, then alert security on-call. Policy: InfoSec-Phishing §2 — every reported phish triggers a same-day takedown attempt and a check for additional victims. Escalate to: security-oncall@example.com (paged via PagerDuty) if any recipient interacted with the email.

input.question: What's the policy on using personal Gmail for work?

expected.answer: Summary: Prohibited — work correspondence must stay in the corporate email tenant. Policy: InfoSec-Email §1.2 — personal email accounts are not under the company's retention, audit, or DLP controls. Escalate to: it-help@example.com for legitimate-need exceptions.

input.question: Can I keep my company laptop after I leave?

expected.answer: Summary: No — all company hardware must be returned within five (5) business days of your final day. Policy: HR-Offboarding §3.2 — IT provides a return-shipping label; cost is borne by the company. Escalate to: it-offboarding@example.com if you need a return-label expedited or extended.

input.question: Am I allowed to take a 6-month sabbatical?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes after five (5) years of continuous service, subject to manager + People Ops approval. Policy: HR-Leave §8.1 — sabbaticals are 6 weeks (paid) or up to 6 months (unpaid); approval considers business need and team coverage. Escalate to: People Ops with proposed dates at least ninety (90) days before the intended start.

input.question: Can I work from another country for the summer?

expected.answer: Summary: Up to ten (10) consecutive business days per trip is auto-approved in our pre-approved countries; longer stays require People Ops review. Policy: HR-Remote-Travel §3.1 — submit a travel-notify form seven (7) days in advance. Escalate to: People Ops for stays >10 days or in non-approved jurisdictions.

input.question: Can I sign an NDA on behalf of the company?

expected.answer: Summary: No — NDAs require Legal countersignature regardless of dollar value. Policy: Legal-Contracts §1.1 — only authorized signatories may execute company agreements. Escalate to: legal@example.com to route the NDA through the standard review queue (24-hour SLA).

input.question: How do I get the company W-9 sent to a customer?

expected.answer: Summary: Customer-success can email the standard W-9 PDF directly. Policy: Finance-Documents §2 — the W-9 is non-sensitive and may be shared with any verified counterparty. Escalate to: finance@example.com for a customer-specific request (e.g. accompanying letter or wet signature).

input.question: Can I attend a competitor's user conference?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for industry intelligence purposes after manager notification. Policy: HR-Conduct §3.5 — attendance must not include sharing of internal information. Escalate to: comms@example.com if you'll be on a public panel or quoted in published materials.

input.question: Is it okay to use my personal phone for two-factor authentication codes?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for personal/professional logins; corporate admin actions require a managed device or hardware key. Policy: InfoSec-MFA §1 — TOTP codes on personal phones are acceptable for standard SSO; privileged actions need MDM-enrolled device or YubiKey. Escalate to: it-help@example.com to be issued a hardware key.

rationale: Tiered yes/no with concrete next step.

input.question: Can I disclose my salary to a colleague?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes — sharing your own compensation is protected speech. Policy: HR-Compensation §2.4 — the company does not restrict employees from discussing their own pay. Escalate to: People Ops if you believe pay discussions are being chilled or punished.

input.question: How do I dispute a performance review?

expected.answer: Summary: Submit a written rebuttal via the People Ops appeals queue within fourteen (14) days of receiving the review. Policy: HR-Performance §4.3 — the appeal is reviewed by your manager's manager and an HRBP. Escalate to: People Ops if the appeal outcome is contested or you experience retaliation.

input.question: Can I install Homebrew packages on my work laptop?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for the documented allowlist; new packages require IT-Security review. Policy: InfoSec-Endpoint §3.2 — the allowlist is published in the IT portal; off-list installs trigger a DLP alert. Escalate to: it-help@example.com to add a package to the allowlist (24-hour SLA).

input.question: How do I report a coworker for bullying?

expected.answer: Summary: File via the People Ops conduct queue or anonymously via the Ethics Hotline. Policy: HR-Conduct §1.1 — every report is confidential and protected against retaliation. Escalate to: ethics-hotline@example.com (third-party administered) if you prefer external reporting.

input.question: Do I have to use the company VPN when at a coffee shop?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for any access to internal systems; public Wi-Fi is treated as untrusted. Policy: InfoSec-Connectivity §2.1 — the VPN client auto-launches on join to non-corporate networks. Escalate to: it-help@example.com if the VPN won't connect after troubleshooting.

input.question: Can I take a personal call during a meeting?

expected.answer: Summary: At your discretion provided it's brief and you mute/excuse yourself. Policy: HR-Conduct §2.1 — no codified rule; norms expect professional courtesy. Escalate to: your manager for any prolonged or repeated absence pattern.

input.question: Where can I read about our salary bands?

expected.answer: Summary: The compensation philosophy + band ranges are published internally on the People Ops Notion. Policy: HR-Compensation §1.3 — bands are reviewed annually; band placement is private. Escalate to: People Ops for questions about your specific placement.

input.question: Can I expense food for a client dinner I hosted at home?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes up to $150 per attendee with a brief business-purpose note. Policy: Finance-Expense §3.4 — entertainment expenses require attendee list + purpose. Escalate to: finance@example.com for amounts above the per-attendee cap.

input.question: Is it ok to publish a blog post about a customer we worked with?

expected.answer: Summary: No — customer references require written approval from the customer and Comms. Policy: Comms-References §1 — every public mention of a customer is reviewed for accuracy and approval status. Escalate to: comms@example.com with the customer's approval email + draft.

input.question: Can I record a Zoom call without telling participants?

expected.answer: Summary: No — explicit verbal or written consent from every participant is required before recording. Policy: InfoSec-Recording §1 — applies to internal and external calls; some jurisdictions require all-party consent legally. Escalate to: legal@example.com for any cross-border call or potential legal-evidence recording.

input.question: How do I get a security clearance for our defense customer?

expected.answer: Summary: Coordinate with the customer's security officer; the company does not sponsor US clearances directly. Policy: Legal-Compliance §6 — we work with cleared partners through subcontracting. Escalate to: legal@example.com to set up a sponsoring-partner arrangement.

input.question: Can I deploy directly to production from my laptop?

expected.answer: Summary: No — production changes must go through the CI/CD pipeline with peer review. Policy: Engineering-Releases §1.1 — direct prod access is reserved for on-call break-glass scenarios with audit logging. Escalate to: release-managers@example.com if you believe you have an exception need.

input.question: How do I get a contractor onboarded with access to our codebase?

expected.answer: Summary: Contractor must sign the standard NDA + complete security training before any code access. Policy: HR-Contractors §2.1 — the contractor-onboarding flow assigns minimum-necessary permissions. Escalate to: people-ops@example.com to start the contractor onboarding kit.

input.question: What's the policy on accepting LinkedIn endorsements from customers?

expected.answer: Summary: Permitted; no disclosure or approval required. Policy: HR-Conduct §3.7 — public endorsements of skills are individual matters. Escalate to: comms@example.com only if a customer asks you to publicly endorse our product (that requires Comms review).

input.question: Can I bring my friend to the holiday party?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes — the holiday party is plus-one eligible. Policy: People-Events §2 — the RSVP form will ask for plus-one details. Escalate to: events@example.com for accessibility or dietary accommodations.

input.question: How do I file an OSHA complaint anonymously?

expected.answer: Summary: File via the federal OSHA online portal or anonymously via our Ethics Hotline. Policy: HR-Safety §3 — internal and external reporting are both protected; retaliation is prohibited. Escalate to: ethics-hotline@example.com for confidential internal handling.

input.question: Can I use our company logo on my personal portfolio site?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for indicating employment; not for endorsing your services. Policy: Comms-Brand §2.2 — 'I work at X' usage is fine; 'X recommends my services' is not. Escalate to: comms@example.com if your portfolio offers services to potential X customers.

input.question: What's the procedure for a security audit by a customer?

expected.answer: Summary: Audits are conducted by reviewing the SOC 2 Type 2 report + the annual customer-audit packet; on-site or interactive audits require a contract amendment. Policy: Compliance-Audits §1 — the standard packet covers 95% of customer requests. Escalate to: compliance@example.com for any audit requiring custom evidence or on-site access.

input.question: Can I order a 3D-printed prototype on the company card?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes if related to documented R&D work and under $500 — over that requires manager approval. Policy: Finance-Expense §2.3 — research materials follow standard expense policy. Escalate to: your manager for approval >$500 or finance@example.com for unusual vendor onboarding.

input.question: What's the policy on sharing screenshots of our admin dashboard externally?

expected.answer: Summary: Prohibited — admin dashboards contain customer identifiers and pricing data. Policy: InfoSec-DataClassification §2.3 — only sanitized mock data may appear in external materials. Escalate to: comms@example.com for marketing-asset screenshots; security@example.com for any accidental exposure.

input.question: Can I expense a coworking day pass while traveling for work?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes up to $50/day with receipt. Policy: Finance-Expense §4.2 — coworking is a reimbursable workspace expense during business travel. Escalate to: finance@example.com if you need a monthly membership instead of day-pass for an extended trip.

input.question: Do I need to take vacation days for jury duty?

expected.answer: Summary: No — jury duty is paid leave separate from PTO. Policy: HR-Leave §3.5 — submit the jury summons to People Ops; pay continues at regular salary for up to ten (10) business days. Escalate to: People Ops if your service extends beyond ten days.

input.question: Can I post a photo of my office whiteboard to Twitter?

expected.answer: Summary: No — whiteboards routinely contain pre-release or sensitive content. Policy: InfoSec-DataClassification §2.2 — internal artifacts may not be photographed for external sharing. Escalate to: comms@example.com if you want a blurred version reviewed for public posting.

input.question: How do I get reimbursed for an internet bill while working remotely?

expected.answer: Summary: Up to $50/month is reimbursable as a home-office stipend. Policy: Finance-Remote §2 — full-time remote employees may submit one bill per month; receipts must show the billing address matches HR records. Escalate to: finance@example.com for hybrid-employee proration.

input.question: What's the procedure for terminating a contractor's access?

expected.answer: Summary: Manager opens a JIRA ticket in IT-Offboarding; access is revoked across all systems within four (4) business hours. Policy: InfoSec-Offboarding §1.4 — covers SSO, repo permissions, VPN, and physical access. Escalate to: it-offboarding@example.com if any system is missed.

input.question: Can I accept a $200 gift from a vendor?

expected.answer: Summary: Decline or escalate — anything above $100 from an active or prospective vendor requires written approval. Policy: Ethics-Gifts §2 — covers meals, swag, conference passes, and event tickets. Escalate to: compliance@example.com with vendor name and gift description before accepting.

input.question: Can I store training data in our personal Google Drive?

expected.answer: Summary: No — training data must remain in the corporate data warehouse with classification labels. Policy: InfoSec-DataHandling §4 — personal cloud accounts lack our DLP and retention controls. Escalate to: data-governance@example.com if you need expanded access for a specific project.

input.question: How do I add a contractor to our GitHub org?

expected.answer: Summary: Submit a JIRA ticket in IT-Access with the contractor's email, NDA-execution date, and scope of repo access. Policy: Engineering-Access §2 — contractor access is time-bounded and reviewed monthly. Escalate to: it-help@example.com if you need an emergency or expedited add.

input.question: Where do I report a near-miss security incident?

expected.answer: Summary: Report via the security-near-miss channel even if no actual breach occurred. Policy: InfoSec-IR §2 — near-misses inform our control improvements. Escalate to: security@example.com for incidents the on-call should know about now.

input.question: Can I work for a customer of ours on the side?

expected.answer: Summary: No — direct customer engagement creates conflict-of-interest risk. Policy: HR-OutsideEmployment §3 — customer-side work is prohibited; reseller / partner engagements need Legal review. Escalate to: People Ops + legal@example.com for any borderline scenario.

input.question: Is it ok to keep paper notes with customer data on my desk?

expected.answer: Summary: No — printed customer data must be locked in a desk drawer when unattended. Policy: InfoSec-PhysicalSec §4 — clean-desk policy applies to all printed sensitive material. Escalate to: facilities@example.com if you don't have a lockable drawer.

input.question: Can I quote a customer's CEO in our marketing without permission?

expected.answer: Summary: No — every quote requires the named individual's + their company's written approval. Policy: Comms-References §2 — even public statements need explicit go-ahead for marketing use. Escalate to: comms@example.com with the proposed quote draft + the customer's approval email.

input.question: What's the policy on bringing my pet to the office?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for the SF office (Tuesdays and Thursdays only) with prior registration. Policy: Workplace-Pets §1 — pets must be on a leash, current on vaccinations, and approved via the pet-roster form. Escalate to: office-sf@example.com to register a new pet.

input.question: How do I file a worker-compensation claim?

expected.answer: Summary: Notify People Ops within 24 hours of the incident; HR initiates the WC claim with our insurance carrier. Policy: HR-Safety §2 — applies to all on-the-job injuries regardless of severity. Escalate to: People Ops immediately; do not delay for any reason.

input.question: Can I install a Slack bot in our workspace?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes after IT-Security review; new apps go through a 5-day review SLA. Policy: InfoSec-SaaS §2 — Slack apps are evaluated for permissions and vendor risk. Escalate to: it-help@example.com to submit a Slack app for review.

input.question: Where do I get my parking validated?

expected.answer: Summary: Reception desks in each office validate visitor parking; employees with parking benefits use the assigned permit. Policy: Workplace-Parking §1 — employee parking is per office; visitor parking requires same-day validation. Escalate to: facilities@example.com if you're missing a permit or need a guest pass.

input.question: Can I email customer data to our outside auditor?

expected.answer: Summary: No — auditor access goes through the secure data room only. Policy: Compliance-Audits §2.1 — never email customer-identifying data; the data room provides access logs + watermarking. Escalate to: compliance@example.com to set up the auditor in the data room.

input.question: How do I get a desk in the office for my onboarding week?

expected.answer: Summary: Reserve via the desk-booking tool — your manager pre-books the first three days. Policy: Workplace-Hotdesk §1 — applies to all hybrid and visiting employees. Escalate to: facilities@example.com if you can't see availability for a specific date.

input.question: What's the policy on cryptocurrency payments to contractors?

expected.answer: Summary: Not currently permitted — all contractor payments must clear through approved corporate banking. Policy: Finance-Payments §1.3 — applies regardless of jurisdiction or payment-platform availability. Escalate to: finance@example.com if a contractor specifically requires non-USD or DeFi rails.

input.question: Can I delete a Slack message that contains a typo with someone's name?

expected.answer: Summary: Slack messages older than seven (7) days are immutable for retention reasons; recent messages may be edited but not deleted. Policy: Records-Retention §5.4 — applies to DMs and channels. Escalate to: it-help@example.com for legitimate redaction needs.

input.question: How do I get an OSS license approved for a new dependency?

expected.answer: Summary: Submit the package + license to the OSS-review JIRA queue; review SLA is two (2) business days. Policy: Legal-OSS §1 — copyleft licenses (GPL, AGPL) require additional sign-off; permissive licenses (MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD) are typically auto-approved. Escalate to: oss-review@example.com for blocked or expedited requests.

input.question: What do I do if I accidentally CC'd a customer on an internal-only thread?

expected.answer: Summary: Immediately reply-all with a recall request, notify your manager, and file a P3 incident in the privacy queue. Policy: InfoSec-DataLeak §3.2 — the privacy team determines whether GDPR Article 33 notification is triggered. Escalate to: privacy@example.com within fifteen (15) minutes of discovery.

input.question: Can I work a second job at another tech company?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for non-competing roles after written manager + HR approval. Policy: HR-OutsideEmployment §2 — competing roles in our defined market segment are prohibited; non-tech side income (teaching, consulting in unrelated fields) generally does not require approval. Escalate to: People Ops with the outside-employment form.

input.question: Do I need to retain my draft documents in Google Drive forever?

expected.answer: Summary: No — drafts older than ninety (90) days that are not under litigation hold may be deleted. Policy: Records-Retention §4.4 — applies to personal drafts in Drive and Notes; collaborative team docs follow stricter retention. Escalate to: legal@example.com if a draft is associated with an open matter.

input.question: How should I respond to a LinkedIn connection request from a competitor's recruiter?

expected.answer: Summary: Connecting is fine; do not share internal information or accept calls without notifying your manager. Policy: HR-Conduct §3.7 — outside recruiting outreach is allowed; disclosure of internal plans is not. Escalate to: People Ops if you receive a formal offer or non-public information request.

input.question: What's the policy on AI-generated code in our repos?

expected.answer: Summary: Permitted for clearly-marked snippets in non-customer-facing tooling; production paths require human review and CI-passing tests. Policy: Engineering-AICode §1 — every AI-generated function must include an author comment and pass standard PR review. Escalate to: ai-governance@example.com for full-file generation review.

input.question: Can I expense my home office desk?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes — up to $1,000 lifetime stipend, plus one $300 refresh every three (3) years. Policy: Finance-Remote §4 — receipts must show the purchase date and the buyer's name matches HR records. Escalate to: finance@example.com for non-standard ergonomic equipment (standing desks, specialized chairs).

input.question: How long do I have to respond to a customer GDPR data-subject request?

expected.answer: Summary: Initial acknowledgment within seventy-two (72) hours; substantive response within thirty (30) days. Policy: Privacy-DSAR §2 — applies to all EU/UK customers regardless of plan tier. Escalate to: privacy@example.com immediately upon receipt — do not respond directly without legal sign-off.

input.question: Can I bring my partner to the company off-site?

expected.answer: Summary: No — off-sites are employee-only unless explicitly designated as 'plus-ones welcome'. Policy: People-Events §1 — the off-site invite specifies plus-one status; default is employees-only. Escalate to: events@example.com to confirm or request an exception.

input.question: What's the procedure for sharing customer references with prospects?

expected.answer: Summary: Coordinate via Customer Marketing; never share contact info directly. Policy: Sales-References §1 — reference customers opt-in to specific call types. Escalate to: customer-marketing@example.com to request a reference call match.

input.question: Can I attend a hackathon and have my work published as open-source?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes if the work is unrelated to your day-to-day duties and competes with no company products. Policy: Legal-Inventions §2 — outside hackathon work is yours subject to the IP-assignment carve-out. Escalate to: legal@example.com to confirm the project doesn't overlap with our IP.

input.question: How do I get a budget increase approved for my team?

expected.answer: Summary: Submit a budget-amendment proposal via Finance Ops with justification and projected ROI. Policy: Finance-Budget §3 — quarterly amendments are reviewed by the FP&A committee. Escalate to: finance@example.com with the proposal at least four (4) weeks before quarter close.

input.question: Can I have a 1:1 with a board member to share product feedback?

expected.answer: Summary: Through your manager or our Board liaison only — direct outreach is not permitted. Policy: Governance-BoardComms §1 — protects the board from informal channel noise. Escalate to: chief-of-staff@example.com if you have a topic that warrants board attention.

input.question: What's the policy on visiting a customer in person?

expected.answer: Summary: Permitted with manager + customer-success approval; submit a travel itinerary in advance. Policy: HR-Travel §2 — applies regardless of distance. Escalate to: customer-success@example.com to coordinate the visit and review pre-meeting materials.

input.question: Can I use my company credit card for personal purchases by accident?

expected.answer: Summary: Reimburse the company immediately via the expense-correction tool; flag the entry as 'personal' in the report. Policy: Finance-Cards §3 — accidental personal use is not a violation if promptly reimbursed. Escalate to: finance@example.com if the purchase exceeds $500.

input.question: How do I request a transfer to a different team?

expected.answer: Summary: Discuss with your current manager first; then submit the internal-transfer form via People Ops. Policy: HR-Transfers §1.2 — transfers require six (6) months of tenure in current role and manager approval on both sides. Escalate to: People Ops to mediate if either manager declines.

input.question: Can I attend a paid conference and consider it work time?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes — pre-approved conferences are work time; manager confirms in the L&D system. Policy: HR-Learning §2 — up to ten (10) conference days per year are paid. Escalate to: your manager to confirm conference inclusion in the L&D budget.

input.question: What's the procedure for accepting a stock option grant?

expected.answer: Summary: Sign the grant agreement via DocuSign within thirty (30) days of issuance. Policy: HR-Equity §1 — unsigned grants expire after the window. Escalate to: people-ops@example.com if you have questions about cliff, vesting, or tax implications.

input.question: Can I review my own performance with my reportees?

expected.answer: Summary: No — review your own performance separately from reportee 1:1s. Policy: HR-Performance §3 — manager-employee performance discussions are kept separate from peer reviews. Escalate to: People Ops for guidance on the right cadence and structure.

input.question: How do I report a wage discrepancy?

expected.answer: Summary: Notify People Ops with your latest paystub and any supporting documentation. Policy: HR-Compensation §5 — discrepancies are investigated and corrected, including back-pay if applicable. Escalate to: People Ops; if not resolved within fourteen (14) days, contact the Ethics Hotline.

input.question: Can I take a personal day with no notice?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes — same-day notification to your manager is acceptable. Policy: HR-PTO §2.3 — same-day PTO is allowed for sick leave, family emergencies, or personal needs. Escalate to: your manager via Slack/email; People Ops if the absence pattern needs HR coordination.

input.question: How do I report a hostile-work-environment claim?

expected.answer: Summary: File via the People Ops complaints channel or anonymously via the Ethics Hotline. Policy: HR-Conduct §1.1 — all claims are confidential and protected from retaliation. Escalate to: ethics-hotline@example.com for external administration.

input.question: Can I publicly criticize a competitor on social media?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes within professional norms; avoid factual claims you cannot defend. Policy: HR-SocialMedia §2 — opinions are yours; misrepresentations of competitors create legal exposure. Escalate to: comms@example.com for any post involving competitor pricing, products, or specific people.

input.question: What's the policy on referring a former colleague to a job here?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes — the referral program is open to current employees with a $5,000 bonus on hire. Policy: HR-Referrals §1 — referral bonus paid 90 days after the referred employee's start date. Escalate to: recruiting@example.com to officially log the referral.

input.question: Can I work from a country with a 6-hour time difference?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for short stays (≤10 days); long-term remote across major time zones requires People Ops review. Policy: HR-Remote-Travel §3.2 — your manager confirms team-coverage feasibility. Escalate to: People Ops with proposed dates + coverage plan for stays >10 days.

input.question: How do I request a hardware upgrade for my laptop?

expected.answer: Summary: Submit a JIRA ticket in IT-Hardware with the desired specs and a brief justification. Policy: IT-Hardware §1.3 — upgrades are evaluated against the company hardware refresh cycle (every 36 months). Escalate to: it-hardware@example.com if your current device blocks your work right now.

input.question: Can I list our customer's logo on my LinkedIn?

expected.answer: Summary: Only if the customer is publicly identified as ours. Policy: Comms-References §2 — non-public customers cannot be referenced. Escalate to: comms@example.com to verify customer's public-reference status.

input.question: Where do I find our certificate of insurance?

expected.answer: Summary: Available in the Finance portal under 'Vendor Documents'. Policy: Finance-Documents §3 — the COI is updated annually with our carrier. Escalate to: finance@example.com if a customer needs a customized COI with their company named.

input.question: Can I attend an investor meeting as an employee?

expected.answer: Summary: Through the CFO or IR team only — direct investor outreach is not permitted. Policy: Governance-InvestorRelations §1 — applies to all current and prospective investors. Escalate to: ir@example.com if you have a topic that warrants investor visibility.

input.question: How do I report a data breach by a vendor?

expected.answer: Summary: File a P1 incident with security and notify the vendor's contact. Policy: InfoSec-Vendor §3 — vendor breaches trigger our own customer-notification review. Escalate to: security@example.com immediately; legal@example.com for the contractual implications.

input.question: Can I keep severance to fund my next venture?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes — severance is yours to use as you see fit. Policy: HR-Severance §1 — payment is unrestricted but contingent on signing the separation agreement. Escalate to: People Ops if you have questions about non-compete or trade-secret obligations.

input.question: What's the policy on contributing to open-source projects in my personal time?

expected.answer: Summary: Permitted for non-competing projects; disclose major commitments to your manager. Policy: Legal-IP §2.1 — your personal projects are yours subject to the IP-assignment carve-out. Escalate to: legal@example.com if you maintain a project that intersects with our product domain.

input.question: Can I attend a court hearing as a witness on company time?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes — court appearances as required by subpoena are paid time. Policy: HR-Leave §4 — submit the subpoena to People Ops; no PTO is deducted. Escalate to: People Ops if you receive a subpoena requiring company-confidential information.

input.question: How do I manage a customer escalation that's now a CSM-level issue?

expected.answer: Summary: Loop in the assigned CSM and route through the executive-escalation queue if VP-level attention is needed. Policy: Sales-Escalation §1 — escalations have defined response SLAs by tier. Escalate to: cs-escalations@example.com with a brief situation summary.

input.question: Can I take my company laptop home permanently?

expected.answer: Summary: Yes for hybrid/remote employees — the laptop is your primary device. Policy: IT-Hardware §2 — devices are inventoried + remain company property. Escalate to: it-hardware@example.com if your role changes and you need to return or replace the device.

input.question: What's the policy on filming videos in the office?

expected.answer: Summary: Permitted in common areas with bystander consent; restricted areas (engineering pods, security desk) require Facilities approval. Policy: Comms-Filming §1 — applies to recruitment videos, social posts, and customer-facing recordings. Escalate to: comms@example.com to coordinate filming in restricted areas.

input.question: Can I work for free for an open-source foundation while employed here?
